matches.rationale: GT 1 concerns an overstated claim in the abstract about performance improvements. None of the findings identify this specific abstract claim or its exaggeration; the findings focus on technical inconsistencies and methodological issues rather than rhetorical overstatement in the abstract.

GT 2 concerns fabricated future citations (2024-2025) in the Introduction presented as established work. Pred 7 mentions citation issues with Vastola (2025) but focuses on misattribution of claims rather than the fabrication of future references as established literature.

GT 3 identifies that Proposition 1's closed-form formula is stated incorrectly without proper normalization (missing softmax). Pred 1 directly addresses this same issue, noting the inconsistency between the softmax normalization description and equation (6)'s presentation.

GT 4 concerns omission of data augmentation reporting in the experimental section. Pred 2 identifies exactly this issue, noting the confusion between Section 3.2 and Appendix D.3 about whether data augmentation was applied.

GT 5 concerns Figure 2's memorization metric being truncated/rescaled and missing error bars. Pred 4 directly identifies this issue, noting the capped vertical axis at 20 and omitted error bars, plus the inconsistency in claiming results are 'within margin of error' without error bars.

GT 6 concerns Proposition 2 incorrectly claiming the Monte Carlo estimator is unbiased when it should be biased. Pred 8 discusses Proposition 2's proof but focuses on the justification of an inequality step, not the bias/unbiasedness claim that GT 6 identifies.

GT 7 concerns overly promotional language in describing Figure 4 results ('consistent modest but steady improvements'). None of the findings identify this specific rhetorical manipulation in the experiments section describing Figure 4.

GT 8 concerns contradiction between the conclusion claiming to 'clarify' generalization while the limitations section admits major unexplored factors. None of the findings identify this specific cross-section inconsistency between conclusion and limitations.
GT 9 concerns omission of thorough privacy risk discussion and mitigation strategies in the broader impact section. None of the findings address ethical or privacy concerns in the paper.
GT 10 concerns understating computational overhead of empirical flow matching in the method section. None of the findings identify this specific claim about computational efficiency being misleading.

GT 11 concerns omission of results for M ≥ 1000 with fabricated justification that they were 'nearly identical.' None of the findings identify this specific data integrity issue about unreported high-M results.

GT 12 concerns promotional language in the related work section ('remarkable agreement,' 'clearly answers'). Pred 7 discusses citation issues but not the rhetorical tone in related work; no finding matches this specific issue.

GT 13 concerns contradiction between Section 3.1 claiming stochasticity is short/unimportant versus earlier emphasis on its importance. Pred 10 identifies this same issue, noting that Section 3.1 draws strong conclusions about stochasticity being overestimated that aren't fully supported until Section 4.
